description:
The only ORM and data access framework for Azure Table Storage in the .NET ecosystem.
ASCDataAccessLibrary gives .NET developers (6 through 10) an Entity-Framework-style experience — lambda expression queries, strongly-typed entities, automatic serialization, batch operations, and fluent extension methods — on top of the most cost-effective NoSQL cloud database available.

v4.3 adds a complete performance layer: a SINGLE unified result cache (one class, one Count, one Clear, one TTL model) with declarative per-entity tuning via [CachePolicy], delta-refresh for append-only data (logs, audit, events) that keeps the cache current at minimal wire cost, SingleFlight coalescing of concurrent identical fetches, paged-result caching, and IAsyncEnumerable streaming for Azure Tables (matching the blob streaming shipped in v4.0). Every existing call site in your codebase gets faster the moment you upgrade — no consumer code change required.

Write idiomatic C# against Azure Table Storage and Azure Blob Storage without touching the raw SDK:
  • var customer = await new Customer().LoadAsync(x => x.CompanyId == id)
  • await customer.SaveAsync()
  • await customers.DeleteAsync()
  • [CachePolicy("5m")] on the entity → process-wide caching with write-through invalidation
  • await foreach (var row in da.StreamCollectionAsync(predicate)) → progressive-render UIs

Key features:
  • Lambda expression queries with automatic hybrid server-side / client-side OData splitting
  • Strongly-typed entities with transparent decimal precision, large string chunking, and enum serialization
  • Dynamic entities (DynamicEntity) for schema-free, runtime-defined data — telemetry, ETL, multi-tenant config
  • Batch insert / update / delete up to any size — auto-chunked at Azure's 100-entity limit
  • Cursor-based pagination with continuation tokens
  • IAsyncEnumerable streaming for Azure Tables — StreamCollectionAsync yields rows as the SDK pages them (NEW in v4.3)
  • Result caching with [CachePolicy] — attribute-driven, TTL-based, write-through invalidation (NEW in v4.3)
  • Zero-config request memoization — auto-creates an AsyncLocal scope on first DAL touch (NEW in v4.3)
  • SingleFlight coalescing — concurrent identical fetches share one Azure round-trip (NEW in v4.3)
  • Azure Blob Storage with IAsyncEnumerable streaming, lambda tag filtering, and FFmpeg video compression
  • Persistent resumable work queues (QueueData<T> + StateList<T>) with crash recovery and position tracking
  • Azure Table Storage session management for ASP.NET Core, desktop, console, and background service apps
  • First-class ILogger provider — standard .NET structured logging backed by Azure Table Storage
  • TableStorage.Configure() once in Program.cs — credentials resolved automatically across the entire app

Built and maintained by Answer Sales Calls Inc. (ASC). Targets Azure.Data.Tables SDK v12 (no legacy Cosmos.Table dependency). Ships as net9.0 — compatible with .NET 9 and .NET 10 SDK builds. .NET 6, 7, and 8 consumers install via NuGet TFM fallback.

Tags: Azure Table Storage ORM, NoSQL database .NET, Entity Framework alternative Azure, Lambda query Azure Storage, Azure data access library, cloud database C#, Azure Blob Storage .NET, result caching .NET, request-scoped memoization, IAsyncEnumerable streaming, SingleFlight coalescing, session management Azure, structured logging Azure Table, queue management .NET, DynamicEntity schema-free storage
releaseNotes:
## Release Notes — ASCDataAccessLibrary v4.3.0 — Performance Layer + Bug Fix Release

### Headline: complete performance layer added in v4.3

v4.3 ships the largest performance upgrade in the library's history. Four new capabilities,
all transparent at the call site, all opt-in or zero-config — no breaking changes, no
consumer code rewrites required.

**1. ONE unified result cache (DataAccessCache)**
v4.3 ships a SINGLE cache class. One dictionary, one Count, one Clear, one TTL model.
Every DAL read path funnels through it automatically — GetRowObjectAsync (every overload,
including the PK+RK shortcut), GetCollectionAsync (every overload), GetCollectionByFilterAsync,
GetAllTableDataAsync, and GetPagedCollectionAsync (each page cached by continuation token).
StreamCollectionAsync bypasses the cache by design (streaming consumers want live data).

Every entity is cached by default — entities without [CachePolicy] use DataAccessCache.
DefaultTtlSeconds (120s by default, set by PollerHost.EnsureStarted on startup). Set to 0
to opt non-policy entities out entirely.

[CachePolicy("5m")] overrides per entity. [CachePolicy("5m", AppendOnly = true)] enables
delta-refresh — on TTL expiry the cache fires a delta query (filter AND Timestamp gt
CachedAt), merges new and updated rows into the existing cached list by RowKey, and bumps
the entry's CachedAt. Append-only tables stay current at minimal wire cost (a few new rows
per refresh instead of the full set). Ideal for AppLoggingData, ErrorLogData, and event-shaped
tables.

[CachePolicy(..., InvalidateOnWrite = false)] disables write-through invalidation for
high-write-rate tables where eviction would defeat the TTL (ShadowPartition uses this).

**2. SingleFlight coalescing of concurrent identical fetches**
When N callers ask for the same query within milliseconds of each other (cold cache, burst
traffic, hot dashboard refresh), the first caller drives the Azure round-trip and the rest
piggyback on the same Task — one Azure round-trip instead of N. Applies to every entity,
with or without [CachePolicy].

**3. Per-table policy registry for DynamicEntity-backed queries**
DataAccessCache.RegisterTablePolicy(tableName, ttl, appendOnly, invalidateOnWrite) sets a
per-table cache policy for queries that can't carry the attribute on the type — DynamicEntity-
backed reads, ETL pipelines, multi-tenant schema-free config. The CCL's HtmlReport widget
calls this against the user's selected table with 5m + AppendOnly so reports are
performant and live new rows surface within each refresh cycle.

**4. IAsyncEnumerable streaming for Azure Tables (StreamCollectionAsync)**
The streaming read surface that has been available for Azure Blobs since v4.0 now exists
for Azure Tables. Three overloads — StreamCollectionAsync(filter), StreamCollectionAsync(
predicate), StreamCollectionByPartitionAsync(partitionKey) — yield rows as the SDK pages
them from the wire. Time-to-first-row becomes one HTTP round-trip instead of the full
materialization wait. All three overloads accept a CancellationToken.

**5. Automatic alias-to-key query rewriting (NEW in v4.3 final)**
Properties whose getters alias PartitionKey or RowKey (the standard CompanyId / CustomerId /
Email-as-RowKey pattern) are auto-detected at first touch and every query against them is
transparently rewritten to target the indexed column. Lambda predicates, structured DBQueryItem
lists, and the field/comparison/value triple all consult the same resolver
(TableEntityTypeCache.ResolveFieldNameForType) so the rewrite is identical across query styles.
Result: identical consumer code, dramatically faster queries (full-table scans become point
reads or partition-bounded scans). Zero risk to non-aliased properties — they emit unchanged.

**BREAKING CHANGE: AppShadowPartitions must be deleted on upgrade**
The shadow catalog used by Any Reporting Tools you wrote and any DataAccess<ShadowPartition> consumer is
repartitioned in v4.3 final: PartitionKey changes from "{tableName}" to "{tableName}:{fieldName}"
so per-field catalog reads hit a small partition instead of one giant table-wide partition.
**Action on upgrade: delete AppShadowPartitions in every storage account.** The catalog
rebuilds automatically as DAL writes resume. Application log/audit tables with reporting
dependencies on the shadow catalog may also need to be wiped + repopulated; CRUD-only consumers
are unaffected. See section 27 of the getting-started guide.

**Caveat: external writes**
Azure Table Storage has no change feed. Writes that happen outside this process — Azure
portal edits, AzCopy, sibling app instances, manual SQL — are not seen by the cache.
The TTL is the staleness ceiling (default 120s) for those mutations. AppendOnly entities
extend this ceiling for externally-deleted or externally-moved-out rows beyond the TTL
(documented tradeoff). Manual flush: DataAccessCache.Clear() or DataAccessCache.InvalidateTable(name).

**Migration impact: zero.** Every existing call site keeps working. The early-beta
DataAccessRequestCache class was removed — if your code referenced it, see §26 of the
getting-started guide for the one-table mapping to DataAccessCache.

See sections 24 and 25 of the getting-started guide for full coverage including AppendOnly
semantics, per-table registry, worked examples, and the external-write caveat.

### Bug fix — identifier double-quoting in lambda method handlers (CRITICAL on Azure Tables)

Every QueryExtensions method handler — `In`, `Between`, `IsToday`, `IsThisWeek`, `IsThisMonth`,
`IsThisYear`, `InDateRange`, and the OData `StartsWith` branch — plus the standard
`IEnumerable.Contains(x.Prop)` membership test, was emitting property names wrapped in
double quotes (e.g. `"CompanyID" eq 'value'`). Azure Table Storage OData v2 rejects this
with `InvalidInput — Syntax error: character '"' is not valid at position …` because
OData property names are bare identifiers. Ordinary `==` / `!=` / `>` / `<` comparisons
were unaffected because they ran through `VisitMember` → `_memberStrategies`, which
correctly emits bare identifiers.

Net effect of the bug in v4.2 and earlier: any lambda using one of the affected methods
threw `Azure.RequestFailedException` (HTTP 400) at query time on Azure Tables. The
documentation claimed these operators were server-side and "Good" performance; in
practice they failed entirely on the primary backend.

The fix introduces a single `RenderFieldName(MemberExpression)` helper inside
`UnifiedFilterGenerator` that routes every method handler through the same
`_memberStrategies` chain that powers `VisitMember`. Identifiers are now emitted
identically across every code path — bare for OData, and whatever the active strategies
dictate for SQL-style backends (Blob Index Tags continue to receive their legitimate
double-quoted form via the dedicated `Tags["key"]` indexer path, which is unchanged).

No public API changes. No behavior changes for `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`,
`string.IsNullOrEmpty()`, `&&`, `||`, `!`. The fix unlocks correct server-side
execution of the affected operators on Azure Tables — consumers calling
`.In(...)`, `.Between(...)`, `.IsToday()`, etc. immediately start getting results
instead of 400 errors after upgrading.

### v4.2 highlights (for adopters upgrading from older releases)

**Shadow Partition cataloguing — automatic distinct-value awareness**
Every entity write now silently catalogues the unique field values it observes into a
dedicated AppShadowPartitions table. This gives the library — and your application —
the ability to answer "what values exist for this field?" without scanning the data table.
Azure Table Storage has no SELECT DISTINCT or GROUP BY. Shadow Partitions fill that gap.

Key properties of the shadow write path:
  - Fire-and-forget: decoupled from the primary write via Task.Run — zero latency impact
  - Idempotent: process-lifetime ConcurrentDictionary cache means each unique
    (table, field, value) triple hits Azure Storage exactly once per process run
  - O(1) existence checks: deterministic RowKey (MD5 hash of field + value) means
    the cold-path storage check is always GetEntityIfExistsAsync(pk, rk) — never a scan
  - Recursion-safe: ShadowPartition entities are never self-catalogued
  - Filtered by type: string, int, long, double, and enum fields only;
    Guid fields excluded (high-cardinality, not useful as filter catalog);
    string values over 200 characters skipped (free-text, not categorical)

New public API:
  - ShadowPartition entity in ASCTableStorage.Models — query AppShadowPartitions directly
  - DataAccess<T>.GetRowObjectAsync(string partitionKey, string rowKey) — true O(1)
    point read using GetEntityIfExistsAsync; use whenever both keys are known

**Updated getting started guide**
Complete v4.2 documentation included as package readme. Section 23 covers:
  - Shadow Partition architecture and performance characteristics
  - Dynamic filter dropdown population
  - Schema discovery without reading entity data
  - Data quality monitoring for controlled-value fields
  - AI-assisted natural language query context
  - Audit and compliance reporting
  - Multi-tenant configuration discovery
  - Cleanup patterns for schema changes

### v4.1 highlights (for new adopters)
- Single-configure credential model: TableStorage.Configure() once in Program.cs
- No-arg constructors on DataAccess<T>, AzureBlobs, Session, QueueData<T>
- QueueData<T> credential-free static methods
- net9.0 target — compatible with .NET 9 and .NET 10; TFM fallback for .NET 6–8

### v4.0 highlights (for new adopters)
- Migrated from legacy Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos.Table to Azure.Data.Tables SDK v12
- Hybrid query engine: lambda expressions split automatically between server-side OData and client-side filtering
- QueueData<T> + StateList<T> persistent resumable work queues
- Azure Blob Storage with lambda tag filtering and IAsyncEnumerable streaming
- Fail-safe protection against accidental full table scans

See getting-started-guide-43.md for full API documentation and migration guide.
